title: Diagnose the pacman first-hook stall; fix wrapper drift, finish the guard-lib migration, serialise heavy jobs
objective: pacman intermittently freezes at its first PreTransaction hook (5 abandoned transactions since 2026-07-29, stalls of 4 minutes to overnight). Establish what is actually failing rather than assuming, then repair the real deployment defects found along the way. Success means: the stall is either root-caused or instrumented so the next real occurrence is captured; the deployed pacman wrapper matches its source and drift can no longer hide; there is one guard system for /etc/hosts instead of two half-installed ones; and concurrent heavy jobs on this 7.6 GB machine are prevented by a mechanism rather than by a human remembering a rule.
acceptance_criteria: The guard-lib hook is proven not to be the cause (its target list is empty, so the script body cannot execute)
A repro harness drives real pacman transactions and captures /proc/<pid>/stack, wchan, syscall, process tree, meminfo and PSI on a stall
A passive --watch mode captures the same evidence from a real (not synthetic) stall
Deployed pacman_wrapper matches the repo source, and check_and_enable_services.sh detects content drift in both directions (source moved on / deployed tampered) and fails closed when unverifiable

hosts, nsswitch and resolved are guardctl file-guard instances; the legacy pacman hooks and units are retired; /etc/hosts keeps chattr +i, its read-only bind mount, its exact contents and its blocking behaviour
The migration has a --rollback that restores the legacy layer INCLUDING the immutable flag, verified by running it
A heavy-job lock serialises pacman transactions, makepkg builds and the coverage hook, names the current holder when it makes something wait, and always fails open
out_of_scope: Shipping a pacman-side fix for the stall itself: it could not be reproduced, so there is no verified defect to fix yet

The shutdown-schedule guard instance: /etc/shutdown-schedule.conf does not exist on this machine, so registering it would mean installing the midnight-shutdown feature rather than finishing this migration
Wiring the lock into Flutter/Gradle builds: the repo has no single build entry point to wrap; the lock is available as a CLI for those
Anything on the desktop machine, which is not reachable from this session
verifier: sudo diagnose_pacman_hook_stall.sh --runs N [--with-load]; sudo migrate_hosts_guard_to_guard_lib.sh --status/--rollback; sudo check_and_enable_services.sh --status with deliberately induced drift; timed heavy_job_lock.sh contention tests; pre-commit run --files <changed>
